title.narrative: Ecological and Low-Carbon Food Systems in China

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Promote the transformation of agrifood systems in China through low carbon, climate resilient, and environmentally friendly production practices throughout the entire food system in target Provinces, while improving livelihoods and sustainability of important food crops and agricultural products.
Indicator targets: Area of land restored: 90,000 ha; Area of land and waters under improved practices: 1,550,000; GHGs mitigated: 10,395,998 million metric tons CO2eq over 20 years.

The project will ensure that project staff adhere to both national employment and labour laws, as well as international commitments, and will increase the protection and promotion of worker health and safety. This includes providing occupational safety and health training as well as child labour prevention in agriculture. Actions to ensure that social and economic co-benefits flow to project beneficiaries throughout the agrifood system have been mainstreamed throughout project strategies detailed above in Section B. Planning for these investments is based on deep socio-economic analysis undertaken and extensive data collected across the eight target provinces: Hubei, Heilongjiang, Jilin, Liaoning, Ningxia, Anhui, Jiangsu, and Fujian. Within these areas, the study was further refined around selected sample districts and counties where the project will be active, which are considered representative of the provinces within which they are located. Overall, the project will directly benefit at least one million individuals involved in food production and agrifood value chains, and indirectly benefit many more. Based on the above analysis, the project is expected to generate positive socio-economic benefits and enhance the capabilities of all social groups and stakeholders involved. Overall, it is anticipated that the project will result in positive impacts among stakeholders, and conversely, it is not anticipated that negative impacts with regard to any specific social group will result, within or outside the project area. A detailed socio-economic assessment by province and project locality is provided in Annex P.The implementation of the project is expected to encourage the strengthening of agricultural technology and information support in the project area, actively introducing new knowledge and practices, as well as fostering technological innovation and development. The project will also encourage agricultural production and processing enterprises to establish workstations and/or laboratories within their premises and to engage doctoral, post-doctoral, and other academics to undertake research there to advance innovations and help strengthen the capacity of local agricultural technology extension services, while also improving the capacity of local agricultural technology extension centers. This will also increase employment opportunities for local agricultural production extensionists and technicians.Following the successful implementation of the project, it is expected that efforts to attract investment and encourage agricultural enterprises to set up new operations in project areas will gain momentum and become continuous. This influx will increase the number of small to medium scale, as well as large scale, agricultural business entities, and the emergence of these new businesses will help lead to more employment opportunities for local farmers and provide more diverse income generating and employment channels. In addition, the improvement of overall environmental conditions will encourage the development of emerging industries such as rural tourism and rural homestays. This will diversify rural industry types and provide new employment opportunities for local farmers.After the project's implementation, further training will be provided to farmers to leverage the advantages of large-scale mechanization. The goal is to cultivate highly skilled farmers, improve their agricultural production capabilities and basic skills, and enhance their employability. The project is expected to broaden farmers' employment opportunities by promoting the development of specialty agricultural products and supporting the development of secondary and tertiary industries in rural areas.The project also plans to work with local administrations to encourage the development of modern agricultural industrial parks that integrate a variety of functions, including for example modern agricultural seedling development, agricultural product processing, technology research and development, along with new product development and marketing. This approach is also anticipated to boost local investment in the agricultural sector and provide new employment opportunities.The actions outlined above are expected to enhance the resilience of the overall agricultural sector and specific value chains, promote the development of branded agricultural products and related processing, as well as large-scale agricultural product sales marketing. This, in turn, will contribute to increasing agricultural production and farmers' incomes. Additionally, the project is expected to help significantly reduce the use of chemical inputs by farmers, lowering overall agricultural production costs which will result in cost savings and efficiency gains, and ultimately increase farmers' income levels.The project will also focus on assisting farmers and producers to meet farmland management and production standards to enhance farmers' productivity and income levels. Furthermore, the added value of the range of agricultural products supported under the project is anticipated to rise, particularly through improvements in processing and transportation such as cold-chain investments, which will also help boost farmers' income levels. The project will further enhance the development of “digital villages”, integrating with new media approaches to expand farmers' sales methods and provide new income generating and employment generation channels. It is expected that partnerships will be formed with farmer cooperatives and large-scale growers to establish smart farm demonstration sites. These smart farms will serve as a basis for supporting and conducting technical training for rural labor, thereby enhancing farmers' skills and employability. Additionally, as the project's demonstration zones are established and the ecological environment improves, as noted above this will also encourage the development of emerging industries such as rural tourism, rural wellness, and homestays – and support an ongoing process of income diversification.
